title: A grate in a gutter on a grade
process: gutter flow down a kerbed street, and the share of it one grate on the grade takes
executor: node (CPU surface solver) and browser (GPU); raw measurements in street/raw/, scored by run.mjs
equations: gutter (FHWA HEC-22 Eq. 4-2): Q = (0.376 / n) Sx^1.67 SL^0.5 T^2.67; depth at the kerb T Sx; mean depth over the first metre Sx (T - 0.5)

grate on a grade (Eq. 4-16, 4-19, 4-20): frontal share Eo = 1 - (1 - W/T)^2.67, side interception Rs = 1 / (1 + 0.0828 V^1.8 / (Sx L^2.3)), efficiency E = Eo + Rs (1 - Eo), with all the frontal flow taken (velocities below splash-over)
flow reaching the grate at steady state: rain x street width x distance from the top
boundaryConditions: kerb and the other three sides: walls, except the foot of the street, a free-outfall edge; the grate sits on a 0.45 m pipe to a free outfall that never limits it
geometry: half a street 100 x 8 m, cross slope 2 % to a kerb along y = 0, falling 1, 2 or 4 % along its length, n 0.016; one of the app's default grates (0.2 m^2, 2 m weir length, Cw 0.5, Co 0.6) in the kerb cell at 75.5 m; 1 m cells

hec22Grate.unit: m wide, m long, m from the top of the street

aboveX.unit: m: the kerb cell whose depth is scored

cases.unit: slope along the street %, rain mm/h for 20 min

solver: FloodSim surface solver with the app's settings (hdry 1e-5 m, hfront 1e-3 m, dtDry 2 s; MUSCL minmod, HLLC, SSP-RK2, CFL 0.48). cpu rows: src/solver-cpu.js (fp64). gpu rows: src/solver-gpu.js in Chrome WebGPU (fp32). The grate through the production Coupler and SWMM, two-way exchange (the app default).

reference.sources: FHWA HEC-22, Urban Drainage Design Manual, 3rd ed. (2009), sec. 4.3.2 and 4.4.4.1 (opened 17 Nov 2026)
reference.independence: the manual's equations from the street's shape, the rain and a grate size; nothing from the solver or the coupler
reference.crossCheck: refs.test.mjs: the spread against Manning strip by strip; the frontal share against the strip flow over the grate's width

outputs: the share of the flow reaching the grate that it takes (mean over the last 300 s)
the depth in the kerb cell 5 m above the grate at the end
reported: HEC-22's frontal share alone, the depth in the grate's own cell
criteriaNotes: The grate passes if its share is within 10 points of HEC-22's efficiency. The gutter passes if the kerb cell is within 2 mm or 10 % of the manual's depth averaged over that cell. NOT a blind test: these nine runs were first made as an unscored diagnostic (street/diagnostics/gutter.mjs), which showed the grate taking 26 to 40 % against HEC-22's 69 to 92 % and the gutter depth within 1.1 mm. The limits were set afterwards, at values that would have been reasonable beforehand; the case is registered so the result is scored and repeatable, and so a fix can be measured against it.
resolution: 1 m cells: the gutter's triangular section is one cell's mean bed
assumptions: a 0.6 x 0.9 m grate in a uniform gutter section; the app's default grate has no stated width or length, only an area and a weir length
frontal flow all taken (the highest velocity here is 1.0 m/s)
limitations: one cross slope, one street width, one grate size
sheet flow feeds the gutter along its whole length: a real street also has a crown
HEC-22's equations are fits to laboratory tests of grates, with their own scatter
validRange: a grate on a continuous grade of 1 to 4 % in a uniform gutter, spreads of 1.1 to 2.4 m
scoring: automated: street/score.mjs builds rows with lib/score.mjs row(); one row set per executor (cpu, gpu), never merged; a case with no raw file is listed as not run and has no rows

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration; not blind, see criteriaNotes
